Summer Paid Internship - Grant Writing

I-RAISE Internship - Summer Grant Writing Program 
The I-Raise Summer Grant Writing Program is a paid internship to learn and train with the best and the brightest in the industry, while gaining real-world experiences! 

Read on for details; dates, hours, compensation and incentives, travel reimbursement, and a sampling of the topics to be covered in the bootcamp. A laptop will also be provided. 

Application Deadline: March 27 

What is the goal of this internship/program? 

For college students interested in grant work. Statewide professionals will all come together this summer in Ames to engage in a customized grant bootcamp to inspire and train our next generation of grant leaders. 

Full summer commitment for Central student, who must be present at ISU: May 27 through Aug. 7 

This is a new, year-long, cross institutional internship program preparing students across Iowa for high-impact careers in research administration, research development, and compliance. I-RAISE interns will receive classroom training, mentorship, hand-on experience, and connections to a regional research administration community. 

Who can apply: 

Open to students in all disciplines and degree programs at Central College (and other I-RAISE partner institutions.) This internship will be open to one student intern at Central College. 

Printable flyer w/full details, dates, compensation, and topic examples: I-Raise Internship - Summer Grant Writing Program.pdf 

Internship Program Application: Central College I-RAISE Internship Application 

After reviewing the flyer and application, if you have questions, please contact Michelle Wilkie ( wilkiem@central.edu ) or Leslie Duinink ( duininkl@central.edu ).

Inclusive Housing Applications Due Soon!

Inclusive Housing in Nanes (near the library) is open to students who are allies, advocates, and/or exploring their identities. Residents must be active members of a student organization supporting an underrepresented group, submit a reflection each semester, and attend and reflect on one identity-focused campus event per semester.
